Question_text: The diagram shows the fixed costs, variable costs and total costs of a firm at output S. Which distance represents the firm's variable costs?
image: A cost-output diagram. The horizontal axis is 'output' and the vertical axis is 'costs'. A horizontal line from R on the cost axis to S on the output axis indicates fixed costs. A line starting from the origin and sloping upwards represents variable costs. A line parallel to the variable costs line, starting from R on the cost axis, represents total costs. Points P, Q, R, S are marked. At output level S, point R represents fixed costs on the y-axis, point Q is on the variable cost curve, and point P is on the total cost curve. Segment RS represents output S and fixed costs. Segment QS represents total variable costs. Segment PS represents total costs. Segment PQ represents fixed costs (Total Cost - Variable Cost).
